highlights.title: Lions and cheetahs and chimps, oh my: a spotlight on Africa's diverse wildlife
highlights.summary: Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use. Credit: National Geographic. A wild African black panther prowls for prey. An orphaned baby pangolin must learn how to climb on its own.
body: The seven-episode documentary series took four years to complete, with filming taking place across nearly 30 different African countries. Each episode focuses on a specific ecosystem, from the jungle and the desert, to the plains, mountains, and islands of Africa, and closes by spotlighting the various scientists, photographers, and NatGeo explorers whose work made the series possible. The final episode focuses on the local conservation leaders and researchers working to preserve Africa's rich biodiversity for future generations.

The producers found the perfect narrator in Wunmi Mosaku, who has delivered powerful performances in such works as Sinners, Loki, and Lovecraft Country. "I was incredibly honored that they even know my name at Nat Geo," Mosaku told Ars. "It was wonderful to be asked to narrate the series, it means so much to me. As someone who was born in Nigeria and raised in England, I'll take any opportunity I can to reconnect and celebrate this incredible continent where life is so diverse and so extreme and beautiful and relentless and peaceful. I wanted to be a part of that because it's a part of me."
points: Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use.
A wild African black panther prowls for prey.
An orphaned baby pangolin must learn how to climb on its own.
The seven-episode documentary series took four years to complete, with filming taking place across nearly 30 different African countries.

highlights.title: Djokovic creates more history with epic Zverev win at China Open
highlights.summary: Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday.
body: The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing.
With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open.

Djokovic is a record six-time champion in Beijing and had won all 29 of his previous matches at the tournament before returning this year for the first time since 2015, when he defeated Nadal in the final to claim his sixth title.
"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn't feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.

highlights.title: Man of Tomorrow Passed An Important Post-Production Milestone
highlights.summary: Man of Tomorrow's post-production process still appears on track despite all the behind-the-scenes changes at Warner Bros. caused by the merger with Paramount. In fact, director James Gunn recently shared that Man of Tomorrow had passed an important post-production editing milestone.
body: In a visual effects-heavy film like Man of Tomorrow, there's still a lot of work to do after the assembly cut stage beyond trimming unneeded footage. While this confirmation is a fairly minor update in the grand scheme of things, it's still good to know that the movie's post-production process remains on track amid all the major shake-ups at Warner Bros. Its merger with Paramount to create Skydance is imminent, and some major leadership changes are happening as a result.

Notably, Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy, the co-CEOs of Warner Bros. Pictures who helped convince James Gunn and Peter Safran to spearhead DC Studios, are exiting the company. Thankfully for DC fans, Gunn and Safran will remain at the company after the merger. As such, it appears Gunn will see Man of Tomorrow's production through to the end and is actively working on the movie.

Man of Tomorrow is still slated for release in theaters on July 9, 2027. The only other DC Studios movies with firm release dates are Clayface (out on Oct. 23), The Batman Part 2 (out Feb. 18, 2028), and Dynamic Duo (out Sept. 22, 2028).

highlights.title: Does the word ‘Dumbass’ flash up when your husband calls your phone? | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: From ‘Sharon London Sex’ to ‘Trashy Anne’, the names saved in our phones are tiny records of how relationships began. Why erase the evidence? At first glance, it’s such a simple, reasonable ask.
body: Personally, I’ve never got over noticing – on their reality show rather than while lunching – that Kim Kardashian has her mother saved as Kris Jenner instead of, say, Mom. It felt like an extremely revealing detail from the queen of the genre.

The Threads debate raised an interesting question, though: should your contact list be amended and updated, or preserved as a historical artefact? Perhaps the poster is underestimating the warm glow to the heart and soul he subconsciously receives whenever his wife’s name pops up and he’s transported back to the beginning of their unlikely love story. Living app-ily ever after is rare, after all.

Other replies echoed the notion that contacts provoke memories. “I’m coming up on the 10th anniversary of ‘Trashy Anne’ … who I got to know volunteering as bin collectors at a local festival,” said one. Another confided: “My best friend and I met through a mutual friend almost 15 years ago. I’m still ‘Ayannah (Gabby’s friend)’.” The comfort we get from a reminder of these origin stories may be more important than it seems.

highlights.title: An AI couldn’t beat humans at StarCraft, so it decided to cheat
highlights.summary: StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn't top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.
body: When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku, it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules. GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “ deceptive behavior ” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least they haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

highlights.title: The Nvidia Shield TV Is 7 Years Old. It Just Got a $100 Price Hike
highlights.summary: The price of anything with memory is skyrocketing thanks to AI. Aging streaming devices are no exception.
body: The era of generative AI has upended technology supply chains, and there is one ironclad rule in 2026: If it has memory or storage, it’s getting more expensive. Even devices with years-old tech inside are still apparently subject to that unwritten rule. Nvidia has just announced that the Shield TV Pro is getting $100 more expensive, effective immediately.

The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. While it ran an aging Tegra X1+ processor, that was (and still is) fast for a TV media streamer. The device launched at $199.99, with a non-Pro variant at $149.99. The non-Pro Shield has since been discontinued, but the Shield TV Pro lives on at the new $299.99 price.

Nvidia has confirmed that you can blame AI for the higher Shield TV pricing. “Starting October 2, SHIELD Pro will be priced at $299. The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry,” a spokesperson told Ars.

highlights.title: Daryz retains Arc crown with dazzling display
highlights.summary: Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp.
body: Not since the Vincent O'Brien-trained Alleged and Lester Piggott in 1977 and 1978 has a colt managed to defend his title, but once Mickael Barzalona pulled the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz out to make his run the result looked inevitable.

The Prix Foy proved the key form guide, as Daryz beat George Scott's Bay City Roller in that trial and those two filled the same positions again in the main event, with Aidan O'Brien's Diamond Necklace running a fine race in third from stall 16.
Barzalona said: "To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse.
"It was a really tough race, it didn't go as we expected but he showed his talent and that made the difference in the end.

highlights.title: Ghost of Yotei DLC’s Best Boss Fight Stars Giant Murder Bears
highlights.summary: Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara, the new DLC for Sucker Punch’s popular 2025 samurai game, is out now, sending players to a new region, the Ashoro Foothills. It does well in adding new and much-needed layers to Atsu, but in between all that character work is more of the open-world exploration…
body: More bounties become available throughout the DLC’s story, which is about Atsu contending with a gang called the Vipers, villains formerly loyal to the Yōtei Six’s Snake. A few bounties are for the heads of those contending for the Snake’s now-vacant spot in the Yōtei Six. One of them includes the most hilarious boss fight in the whole game, and I barely have to unsheath my katana to beat it.

Echoes of Sekigahara explores the impact the Vipers are having on not just the people of the new region of Ashoro Foothills, but its wildlife too. As such, one of the bounties is for Umakichi the Bear Slayer, a scumbag who has several bears kept in cages. He’ll sic them on his soldiers for “training,” and the boss fight arena is littered with corpses of bears.

Umakichi is a big guy with big weapons, and he doesn’t fight fair; like so many of Yōtei ’s baddies, he’s got a gaggle of goons providing him support for the fight. Thankfully, Atsu isn’t alone either. Umakichi’s lackeys are easily cut down by Atsu, and the new heavy weapons she can use help get the job done fast.

highlights.title: John Cooper Clarke looks back: ‘Getting older sucks – it’s marginally better than being dead’
highlights.summary: The punk poet on his heroin years, dressing like Ronnie Wood, and achieving his boyhood ambition. Born in Salford in 1949, John Cooper Clarke is a poet and author. He cut his teeth in the clubs of Manchester before signing to Epic Records in 1978.
body: This is me dressed up as a cowboy with a hat and six-shooter. Not the full schmear with the chaps and all the rest, but the best I could do. I was crazy about westerns. Still am, actually. My uncle Dennis was the only camera-owning relative at the time, so he would have taken the photo in our apartment above a chemist’s shop in Salford, located on a busy traffic intersection.

My childhood is an ever-fading mystery to me, but somewhere around this time I know I got diagnosed with tuberculosis. Something serious like that takes you out of the world, but once I stopped coughing up arterial blood and scar tissue it wasn’t a problem. I stopped going to school, which was great, and not before I’d learned the rudiments of literacy. Really it happened at an opportune moment in that all that I had any energy to do was read.

highlights.title: Russell 'beyond disappointment' as Wolff 'massively annoyed' by engine failure
highlights.summary: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said he was "massively annoyed" after the late unreliability that delivered a potentially knock-out blow to George Russell's title hopes in the Bahrain Grand Prix.
body: Mercedes had already been experiencing an unexpectedly difficult weekend on F1's return to Sepang with the team outqualified by both Red Bull and Ferrari despite bringing a long-awaited car upgrade.

Although Red Bull's Max Verstappen proved too fast in Sunday's chaotic, twice-delayed race, Mercedes were still on course for second with Kimi Antonelli and third with George Russell when, with five laps to go during the second Safety Car phase, the latter's car was stopped by a suspected power unit failure.
The retirement cost Russell 15 points and saw the British driver slip 84 points behind team-mate Antonelli in the title race with seven rounds left.
"I'm so massively annoyed, and not in a happy place," a frustrated Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

highlights.title: Marjoe Gortner, Preacher and Actor Who Was Subject of Oscar-Winning Doc and Appeared in ‘Earthquake,’ ‘Falcon Crest,’ Dies at 82
highlights.summary: Marjoe Gortner, whose childhood as an evangelical preacher was the subject of the Oscar-winning documentary “Marjoe” and who went on to have a career as an actor, died Friday. He was 82. His wife Susan Magestro told Variety he died in Santa Fe, N.M.
body: Born in Long Beach, California, in an evangelical family, the name Marjoe is a combination of “Mary” and “Joseph.” His parents pushed him to become a child preacher, staging a photo op for the press when he performed a marriage ceremony at 4 years old. The family traveled around the country preaching and soliciting donations, and when Gortner was 16, his father absconded with what was reported to be $3 million in donations.
In his 20s, Gortner became disillusioned with the evangelical movement and became an aspiring actor in New York.

When he was approached by documentarians Howard Smith and Sarah Kernochan, he agreed to let them follow him around on his final revival tour in 1971, partially to help publicize his acting career. The resulting documentary, “Marjoe,” won the Oscar for best documentary. Roger Ebert saw it at the Cannes Film Festival and wrote “The real sleeper this year is ‘Marjoe. It generated the most electric response of anything at the festival.” It attracted considerable attention at the time, though it was later “lost” for many years until Kernochan was able to obtain rights to the film after tracking down the owner.
points: Marjoe Gortner, whose childhood as an evangelical preacher was the subject of the Oscar-winning documentary “Marjoe” and who went on to have a career as an actor, died Friday.
His parents pushed him to become a child preacher, staging a photo op for the press when he performed a marriage ceremony at 4 years old.
The family traveled around the country preaching and soliciting donations, and when Gortner was 16, his father absconded with what was reported to be $3 million in donations.
In his 20s, Gortner became disillusioned with the evangelical movement and became an aspiring actor in New York.

highlights.title: Are my gen X peers the influencers the world has been waiting for? | Emma Beddington
highlights.summary: Their careers are peaking, they’re rich in money and time – and young people think they’re cool. But maybe it’s not as simple as that. ‘Stop sleeping on gen X.” I heard this on TikTok recently.
body: Aged between 46 and 61, gen Xers with proper jobs are peaking, career-wise (although it’s a different story for those out of work, as a report last month on the struggles of over-50s jobseekers made plain). We’re more likely to own homes than the following generations; we’re emerging from the trenches of childrearing and, the argument goes, ready to indulge in some me-time. “If gen X were a country, it would be the world’s second-largest consumer market,” the World Economic Forum reported last year, with gen X women in particular influencing 70% to 80% of all consumer spending.

That makes us great customers – witness the tidal wave of menopause-washed wellness guff (Which? reported last month that many pricey supplements were no better than a cheap multivitamin ) and beauty brands for people suddenly horrified by their necks. But does it give us content-creating clout? We’re supposed to be (or at least meme lore presents us as ) the forgotten generation, low-key, countercultural slackers on the sidelines in the grudge match between millennials and boomers; aspiration and self-promotion aren’t really part of our brand.

body: The home cost him $800, and lets him live how he likes, in nature. It’s also in the middle of a gasfield, not far from the Linc Energy contamination site, down the road from a coalmine and three gas power plants.

Last month came the biggest scheme yet, a $31bn datacentre to power Claude, the large language model developed by global AI giant Anthropic. If built, Australia’s largest datacentre would be about 15 minutes’ drive away from Kanowski’s home, outside Kogan, near Dalby, about 180km west of Brisbane.
In a community that has seen the boom and bust of coal seam gas, the response from many has been the same as Kanowski’s: once bitten, twice shy.
“This is the power of money and the power of greed and shortsighted stupidity,” Kanowski says.

highlights.title: Avengers: Doomsday Poster Highlights One Of The Film's Biggest Mysteries
highlights.summary: A new poster for Avengers: Doomsday was unveiled at Comic-Con Málaga on Oct. 3. Although it reveals nothing new about the film, it spotlights three characters we still don't know much about. Right in time for Halloween, this poster has me wondering who the Latverian Witches really are.
body: The new poster for Avengers: Doomsday shows Doctor Doom at the bottom of a grand staircase, presumably in Latveria. Behind him, he's flanked by three witches, each of whom wears a different color. While people colloquially call these mysterious characters Latverian Witches, Marvel has otherwise revealed little about them.

These characters will seemingly help Doctor Doom execute his grand plan in Avengers: Doomsday, but it feels unlikely they are characters we've never met before. In fact, there are several characters who would make sense as the Latverian Witches.

One simply has to look to the magical corner of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and a lot of sensible candidates emerge. Doctor Strange, Clea, and Scarlet Witch seem like obvious fits, especially as we don't know what they have been up to since Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

I could see Bruce Banner as one, since Doctor Doom kidnaps him at the end of Avengers: Endgame Encore, and Sylvie from Loki would also make sense given her connections to the collapsing multiverse. It's possible, if more unlikely, that Agatha All Along characters like Agatha Harkness, Jennifer Kale, or Death show up as Latverian Witches too.

highlights.title: ‘In The Heart of the South’ Director Wants to Change the Narrative For Indigenous Filmmakers: “You’ve Been Telling Our Stories Forever”
highlights.summary: Nyla Innuksuk's supernatural thriller, where themes of trauma and tragedy come painfully alive, is screening at the Vancouver Film Festival this week.
body: Nyla Innuksuk’s supernatural thriller In the Heart of the South is the latest Canadian indie aiming to reclaim indigenous storytelling and representation in movie theaters.

In the Heart of the South centers on Yura Ivalu, a young Inuk artist played by Anna Lambe (True Detective) who takes Toronto’s art world by storm. But the offer of a big movie deal has Ivalu stuck between two worlds as an indie Canadian producer, The Quiet Loud, encourages her to dredge up a childhood trauma to boost future box office.

And Ivalu’s artistic ambitions only spiral out of control when an estranged childhood friend, Sesi, played by Zorga Qaunaq, shows up in Toronto to crash her glamorous party scene and movie ambitions. Innuksuk underlines the moral dilemma she and other indigenous filmmakers face as Ivalu, beset by deep-seated fears, has to choose between telling stories prized by the Canadian film industry around trauma and tragedy, or going beyond colonial stereotypes to represent her Inuit community and legends with authenticity and truth.
points: Nyla Innuksuk's supernatural thriller, where themes of trauma and tragedy come painfully alive, is screening at the Vancouver Film Festival this week.

highlights.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
highlights.summary: David Robinson used to write the safety reports that accompanied every major model release at OpenAI. This week, he resigned from his position and is now speaking out in an editorial in The Atlantic.
body: It’s understandable if you’re feeling a bit cynical about everyone suddenly coming out of the woodwork to warn about how dangerous the thing they helped build is. They did, after all, make this mess. But that doesn’t mean we should discount their warnings.

Robinson says that the culture in industry is fundamentally broken. That this is a deeper issue than simply slapping a few new rules or regulations on how we handle training models. Silicon Valley has operated with “extreme confidence” and “perpetual sprints,” he says, building bigger and better models with “unimpeded optimism” that ignores or underestimates potential problems.

Given today’s risks, frontier labs need to run like nuclear power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.

Asked directly about that next entry, Inaba declined to give specifics, telling Famitsu only to wait and see.

It's certainly more optimistic than recent conversations - series creator Hideki Kamiya left Platinum in October 2023, saying at the time he'd envisioned Bayonetta as a nine-part saga he may now take "to the grave" with him - and Bayonetta 3 director Yusuke Miyata has also since departed.

highlights.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
highlights.summary: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption. There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: snag one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “permanent underclass”, a…
body: The phrase usually describes a future in which AI automates human jobs. But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

“A lot of people say: ‘Oh, AI is lowering barriers, it’s equalizing the playing field for women,’” said Urvashi Batra, co-founder and CEO of Prioriwise, an AI platform for IT service providers. “I actually think it’s the opposite.”

Batra said people take her less seriously as the founder of an AI company than her male co-founder. When pitching investors, she and her co-founder have learned that they are more likely to get an investment if he does the pitching.

Women made up only about a quarter of new hires in AI roles in the last year, compared to 50% of new hires in non-AI roles, according to a recent report from LinkedIn. In executive roles, that number drops to just 13%. At the same time, LinkedIn’s research shows that women are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption, like customer service, meaning they are also at higher risk for job loss due to AI.
points: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption.
